**10** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/vitest.repo-tests.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **74** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c72ec196236e0f9b267d0ecef7e44d449adf9a87` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3922ecfcc80c2592eeeaebcfed8e54bb154227be` — the merge of head `7ef3c981e689e113b4a31864eb3148de3042ac4f` into base `c72ec196236e0f9b267d0ecef7e44d449adf9a87`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3922ecfcc80c2592eeeaebcfed8e54bb154227be && git checkout 3922ecfcc80c2592eeeaebcfed8e54bb154227be
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c72ec196236e0f9b267d0ecef7e44d449adf9a87 7ef3c981e689e113b4a31864eb3148de3042ac4f && git checkout -B drift-repro c72ec196236e0f9b267d0ecef7e44d449adf9a87 && git merge --no-ff 7ef3c981e689e113b4a31864eb3148de3042ac4f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c72ec196236e0f9b267d0ecef7e44d449adf9a87
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c72ec196236e0f9b267d0ecef7e44d449adf9a87` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · #31967 (Fixes #31898) · 2026-11-09T17:24Z

Head-sha: `7ef3c981`

- **Form:** draft to `main`, under `Fixes #31898`.
  - **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`**, confirmed by this ACCEPT as amendment 6740698912 ruled. `RequestExecutionContextInput.transport` (`@objectstack/core`) becomes a required key typed `{ remoteAddress } | undefined`. Every caller now states the peer address, or states that it hands none. Nothing else narrows.
  - `Metadata-protocol: none`, so every package's changeset is patch. ADR-0087 records it as runtime-interface-only, and the gate verified that.
- **Premise (step 0, `31898-step0.md`, `main` `489f0cea`):** no single seam holds the request. `resolveAuthzContext` → `resolveApiKeyAdmission` sees headers only, and six doors call it directly. Step 0 found 13 key-admitting door sites that write `ip_address_absent: 'not_supplied'`. Twelve are on the card. The 13th, `core` `own-row-delete-routes.ts`, is new. Four listed sites admit no key.
- **Change:** one exported core helper, `credentialUseClientFor`, is the only place the `resolveClientAddress` trust rule is asked.
  - The composition and the six direct doors go through it.
  - Each door hands over only its peer address. Hono routes use the guarded `transportPeerAddressOf(c)`.
  - A throw or a missing authority yields no address. Nothing is fabricated.
  - ⛔ No door reads `X-Forwarded-For` or `X-Real-IP`. `client-address.ts` is unchanged.
  - The four session-only sites state `transport: undefined`.
- **Pins and ablations:**
  - One pin per wired door: its `credential_use` row carries the address and the user agent.
  - A core census over every caller of the three seams (js-comment-mask, registered in `cross-package-test-inputs`).
  - CONTROL: REST, `/mcp` and stdio, runtime and the plugin-audit credential-use suite all pass unchanged.
  - Ablations:
    - The seam drops the address (dist rebuilt and preflighted): all 13 door pins go red.
    - A door drops `transport`, the census misses an entry, or the census count is wrong: the census goes red.
    - Each was restored, and `git diff HEAD` came back empty.
- **Gates:** `check-governed-merges --pr 31967` reports NOT governed, +1444/−72. K = 6 first-parent commits on `main` since the merge base, and a local merge with `main` is clean. dispatch-gates: 96/96 exit 0. tsc over 13 packages and root ESLint exit 0. Dogfood: 443 files passed, 3 skipped. CI on this head: 66 runs, none failed.
- **Landing:** ready and auto-merge in this stroke. On merge: a landing record on #31898 and `pm:dispatched` removed. The card closes through `Fixes`.
